clues: MDMA, also known as Ecstasy or Molly, is a synthetic psychoactive drug that acts as both a stimulant and a psychedelic. It can disrupt the body's temperature control and also triggers this condition.
Schwartz and Bartter published a groundbreaking paper detailing two patients with lung cancer who developed this condition. This was the first description of tumors causing a paraneoplastic syndrome
This condition affects an estimated 5% to 10% of all hospital admissions. You might see it in patients with cancer, stroke, head trauma, or post-operatively

Genetic tracking suggests that the parasite was introduced to South America via bats roughly 7 to 10 million years ago before adapting to other mammals and humans. The earliest detection of a human infection comes from a 9,000 year old pre-Columbian mummy.

Charles Darwin is widely speculated to have suffered from this disease. He recorded being aggressively bitten by the 'Benchuca bugs' while traveling through Argentina. After returning to England, he spent the rest of his life plagued by extreme fatigue, heart palpitations, and intestinal distress.
The causal parasite can live quietly and undetected in a human body for 10 to 30 years before causing severe damage to the heart or digestive system with cardiomyopathy, megaesophagus, or megacolon

Project MKUltra was a top-secret CIA program that used this in research about mind control and behavior modification during the Cold War. Researchers secretly administered this substance to unsuspecting citizens in bars, hospitals, and prisons but did not find that it produced reliable mind control

During the 1950s, psychiatrists used this to stimulate mental states or accelerate psychotherapy, but amid rising public concern, the US criminalized this under the Controlled Substances Act of 1970, classifying it as a Schedule I substance

Unlike mane other Schedule I substances, this does not produce compulsive drug-seeking behavior and is not considered physically addictive. It structurally resembles serotonin and brain imaging research suggests it causes communication between areas of the brain that normally do not interact, leading to profound shifts in time and reality.

Approved by the FDA in 1992, this medication is unique because it is the only prescription drug where the FDA recommends different sex-specific starting doses because women clear this medication from their bodies at a slower rate than men.

A popular internet meme imagines a mischievous walrus that shows up at night when you take this medication, whispering strange, terrible, or nonsensical ideas into your ear. This refers to the strange things you might do while taking the medication, like when Roseanne Barr blamed a racist tweet on this medication. The drug maker, Sanofi, famously retorted that 'while all pharmaceutical treatments have side effects, racism is not a known side effect of any Sanofi medication.'
Use of this non-benzodiazepine medication makes up approximately 35-40% of the worldwide sedative market. It is known for causing complex sleep behaviors and next day impairment.
